Cocora

A mobile app where girls can open up to each other without fear of being judged.

  • Mobile app
  • Product design
  • UX research
  • Design system
#A7B9A1#323D2F#60705A
Role
Solo designer
Duration
2 months
Audience
Women only
Tools
Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator

The problem

Many girls hold back from talking about personal struggles because they fear being judged. They need a place to talk about specific life problems with girls who understand.

How I researched it

I studied what girls need, asked people close to me and collected real experiences. I built personas, user flows and wireframes before designing any screen.

The key decision: Cocora is a character, a loyal friend who stays with the user inside the app.

The solution

Cocora guides each girl through the app. If she is unsure in a chat, she can ask Cocora anything, and the answer comes from the team or the in-app AI chat.

What’s inside

Voice verification at sign-up keeps the space girls only. Supervised live voice rooms cover specific topics. The home screen adds a mood check-in and a smart assistant. A design system keeps every screen consistent.

The result

Girls who tried the app said they had needed something like it for a long time, and they connected with the Cocora character.

Khedma

A mobile app that connects customers with skilled workers across Egypt.

  • Mobile app
  • Marketplace
  • UX research
  • UI design
#E19113#059669#FEF3C7
Role
Solo UI/UX designer
Duration
3 months
Users
Customers and tradespeople
Tools
Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator

The problem

Egypt’s informal labor market, with its trades and craftspeople, has a big gap. Customers struggle to find the right worker, and workers struggle to find steady work.

The idea

Reach both sides through one simple mobile app. It had to be easy enough for tradespeople to use, so I kept every flow short and clear.

The key decision: Khedma covers all of Egypt and many trades from day one, so a customer can find almost any worker in one place.

The solution

Customers browse trades, from construction and finishing to mechanics and car services. They choose a nearby worker and send a request. Workers publish their service with a form that sets their price and availability.

What’s inside

Each worker has a profile with location, experience, completed jobs and reviews, so customers can judge if the worker fits the job. Requests turn into a chat, and workers get a dashboard with incoming requests and monthly income.

The result

The app connects both sides. Customers find the right worker, and workers find jobs.

Dalil

A mobile app that helps people plan a metro ride and book their ticket without crowds or cash.

  • Mobile app
  • UX research
  • UI design
  • Academic project
#202F4B#E3E3E3
Role
UI/UX designer
Platform
Mobile app
Focus
Metro riders
Tools
Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator

The problem

Metro stations get crowded, and many riders still pay in cash. People who don’t know the network end up asking strangers how to get from one station to another and where to change lines, and the answers often confuse them.

The idea

An app that lets people book metro tickets from their phone, which avoids queues and cuts cash payments. It also shows each rider where to board, where to get off and where to change lines.

The key decision: show the whole trip before the user pays, with the time, the number of stations, the price and the exact line.

The solution

The rider picks a start and an end station and sees the trip summary first. Then they book, pay with Vodafone Cash or a bank card, and receive a QR ticket for the gates.

What’s inside

A route view lists every stop on the line with its direction. A metro map shows the services next to each station, so riders can choose where to get off. The app also finds the station nearest to the rider’s location.

MOVVA

A ride-sharing app that matches drivers who have empty seats with passengers going the same way.

  • Mobile app
  • Graduation project
  • UX research
  • UI design
#4B0082#440D79#F8E5FF#EBEBEB
Role
Team member, UX and UI
Project
Graduation project
Users
Passengers and drivers
Tools
Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator

The problem

Many car owners drive long distances with empty seats and carry the full fuel cost alone. At the same time, many passengers pay extra fares for trips to the same destination.

How we researched it

Our team ran many interviews and mapped every step of the user experience. Everyone worked on every area, so each of us trained on the whole process.

The core idea: a driver who is already going that way can lower the price, and the passenger still arrives for less than the usual fare.

The solution

Passengers choose a trip type, set the fare they propose, pick a departure time and a seat, and then receive offers from drivers. Drivers go online, see requests, and can accept or raise the fare.

What’s inside

Drivers get an earnings overview and can add scheduled trips to fill empty seats. An emergency screen offers police, ambulance, live location sharing and trusted contacts. Every trip ends with a summary and a receipt, and a trip log keeps the history.
